key_insight: Chemical detections can be traced backward through the flow to infer likely source locations via a learned transport-based path model.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified, Galilean-invariant framework for source localization in turbulent flows that can improve search and detection systems such as olfactory robotics or environmental monitoring.
method: Model concentration detections as evidence of tracer paths from source to sensor.
Use a Schrodinger bridge / backward propagator to sample candidate emission locations.
Run Langevin dynamics to infer the most plausible source positions from observed detections.
evidence_signal: In 2D turbulence tests for olfactory search, the learned backtracking strategy outperformed classical methods across different wind regimes using a single propagator.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurately learning the backward transport model, which may be sensitive to flow nonstationarity or sparse/noisy detection data.
paper_title: Learning Backward Transport for Source Localization
